gaps: UNIVERSE EXCLUDES NON-TS CONSUMERS. The searched universe is exactly the 208 git-tracked files matching `git ls-tree -r --name-only 06d9f8ce172dada98f307f860e2e2985c9fb5ca6 | grep -E '^web/src/.*\.(ts|tsx)$'`, which reconciles with the declared baseline of frontend_files=208. `.css`, `.png`, `.html`, `.svg` under web/src are excluded by that glob, and so is everything outside web/src. A symbol consumed ONLY from web/index.html or another HTML entry point, a CSS module or class-name string, web/vite.config.js, web/playwright.config.*, a Playwright spec outside web/src, a package.json script, or any Go template is INVISIBLE to every count in this map. A zero here is a zero within web/src TS/TSX, never a zero in the application.

REFERENCE COUNTS ARE TEXTUAL, NOT SEMANTIC. No TypeScript program was constructed and no type checker was consulted. Counts come from word-boundary regex over comment-stripped source. This resolves neither shadowing, nor destructuring rebinds, nor property access that happens to share a declaration's name (`x.Button`), nor member names on unrelated objects. Treat every count as an upper bound on real references and a lower bound only if the exclusions above do not apply.

IMPORT AND RE-EXPORT LINES ARE EXCLUDED FROM external_refs BY DESIGN, AND COUNTED SEPARATELY. `external_refs` counts distinct comment-stripped lines outside the defining file that match `\bNAME\b` and are NOT part of an import statement and NOT part of an `export ... from` re-export. The excluded counts are stated verbatim in each record's `note`. This is the deliberate handling of the barrel-re-export trap: barrel lines land in `registration_sites`, so a symbol re-exported from web/src/react/ui/index.ts, web/src/react/hooks/index.ts, web/src/js/api/index.ts, or web/src/types/campaigns/index.ts does not get free reference credit. A consumer reading these records must not add the note's numbers back into external_refs without deciding whether a binding counts as a use.

JSX AND CALL SITES ARE COUNTED ONCE, PER LINE, NOT PER OCCURRENCE. A word-boundary search for the bare name catches `<Foo />`, `</Foo>`, and `Foo(` alike; counting distinct (file, line) pairs rather than regex matches avoids the triple-count the brief warns about. The cost is the converse: two genuinely separate uses of a symbol on one line count as one.

DEFAULT EXPORTS ARE RESOLVED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY NAME. A default export has no stable name at the import site. For every default-exported record the module graph was resolved (relative specifiers against the importer's directory, trying `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.tsx`) and the `note` states how many default-import bindings resolve to that module and names any binder identifier that differs from the declared name. Both declaration forms are covered: `export default function Foo()` and a separate `export default Foo;` statement. The generator also handles a fully anonymous default export (`export default function () {}`), which would carry `identity` `(anonymous default export)` and be counted purely by resolved default-import bindings; no such declaration exists at this baseline, so no record of that shape appears.

LAZY import() SITES ARE RECORDED AS REGISTRATION, NOT AS REFERENCES. web/src/react/App.tsx:22-28 loads all seven route pages via `lazy(() => import('./pages/...'))`. That binds each page module's default export with no identifier whatsoever, so no name search can see it. Those sites appear in `registration_sites` on the corresponding default-export records with an explanatory `note`. A route page therefore legitimately shows a low or zero `external_refs` while being fully live; do not read those numbers without reading the note.

ROUTES ARE COUNTED BY PATH LITERAL, NOT BY COMPONENT. The 14 `route` records come from `<Route path="...">` in web/src/react/App.tsx. Their `external_refs` is the number of other lines in web/src quoting the same path string (nav config, keyboard shortcuts, redirect targets, tests) — it is NOT a measure of whether the route's element component is reachable. Route paths are also assembled elsewhere by string concatenation and template literals, which this literal match does not catch.

TYPE-ONLY REFERENCES ARE COUNTED AS REFERENCES. `import type` bindings are erased at runtime but are real usage, and are treated identically to value references throughout. Conversely, the map does not distinguish a type-only consumer from a value consumer; a `type` record with a nonzero count may have no runtime footprint at all.

TOP-LEVEL DECLARATIONS ONLY. Only declarations beginning at column 0 are enumerated. Nested declarations (functions inside functions, methods on classes other than the APIClient prototype methods described below, object-literal members, and members of `interface`/`type` bodies) are NOT records. This bounds the map at 894 records; an exhaustive member-level census would be an order of magnitude larger and was not attempted. A reconciliation pass (AUDIT_MISSED=1) confirmed that every unmatched column-0 line carrying a declaration keyword is either an `export default Foo;` restatement of an already-recorded declaration or a `declare module './client'` block header, so no top-level declaration is missing.

APIClient METHODS COME FROM DECLARATION MERGING, AND THEIR IMPLEMENTATIONS ARE NOT SEPARATELY RECORDED. The 72 `api-client-method` records are parsed from the `declare module './client' { interface APIClient { ... } }` blocks in web/src/js/api/{campaigns,campaignPurchases,campaignAnalytics,campaignImports,admin,psaCampaigns}.ts. Each is attached at runtime by a `proto.NAME = ...` assignment in the same file, which is why `external_refs` excludes the defining file: the implementation line would otherwise self-credit every method. Call sites are `api.NAME(...)`, which the bare-name search does catch. web/src/js/api/index.ts imports these modules purely for that prototype-augmentation side effect; those side-effect imports are the frontend analogue of Go's `init()` wiring and are not reference evidence.

NAME COLLISIONS ARE FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED. 64 records have `name_ambiguous: true`, meaning two or more top-level declarations in the tree share the bare name; `distinct_definitions_for_name` gives the count and the `note` lists up to six defining sites. The commonest shape is a page component declared once in web/src/react/pages/ and again as a `lazy(...)` const in web/src/react/App.tsx. For every ambiguous record the counts CANNOT tell which definition a given site refers to, and a downstream lens must disambiguate by hand before drawing any conclusion.

MODULE-LOCAL DECLARATIONS ARE INCLUDED AND MARKED. Non-exported top-level declarations are recorded, with a `note` saying so. For these, any external match is by definition either a different symbol or a collision, so a nonzero `external_refs` on an unexported record is noise, not usage.

TEST FILES ARE PART OF THE UNIVERSE. `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx` files under web/src are searched, and 39 records whose every external reference comes from a test file carry `test_only: true`. Test-only usage is usage, and is separately a finding of a different kind — but that judgment belongs to a later phase, not here.

STRING LITERALS ARE NOT STRIPPED. Comments (both `//` and `/* */`) are blanked before matching, so JSDoc mentions do not inflate counts. String and template-literal contents are deliberately preserved, because route paths, query keys, and CSS class names are real references — at the cost that a symbol name appearing incidentally inside prose in a string literal counts as a reference.

NO REACHABILITY CLAIM IS MADE ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP. Per the audit protocol, reachability is not computed by this scout. Every record is a count and a set of sites. Nothing here asserts that any symbol is dead, unused, misnamed, or wrong, and a zero `external_refs` is not such an assertion.
